evidence: Traupman 131: how much is this?, quantī hoc cōnstat?
terms.grammar: phrase: the genitive of price, quantī
terms.comment: The price asked about is in the genitive, quantī, with cōnstat, emis, vēndis; so are tantī, plūris, minōris. A price named is in the ablative: magnō, parvō, asse (see cost a lot).

phrases.latin: Tum pater eam interrogāvit: «Quantī cōnstant?» Pretiō audītō nummōs dēnumerāvit, vēnditrīx nummulōs reddidit.
phrases.english: Then Dad asked her, “How much are they?” When he heard the price he counted out the money, and the stallholder gave back the change.

phrases.latin: dīc quotus et quantī cupiās cēnāre
phrases.english: tell me how many of you there will be, and at what price you want to dine
I don’t buy regret at that price
